activities.title: Pause and check a thought
activities.description: Practise questioning a thought that makes gambling feel appealing.
steps: Name one gambling thought you have noticed. Think it through or write it on paper.
Ask: what supports this thought, and what facts challenge it?
Imagine a friend had this thought. What balanced advice would you give them?
Put that advice into one sentence you can use yourself. Read it slowly.
Choose one helpful action for the next few minutes, such as making a drink or contacting someone you trust.

activities.title: Challenge the 'due a win' thought
activities.description: Recognise a common thinking trap in games with independent random outcomes.
steps: Notice whether you are expecting a win because of earlier losses.
For independent random events, earlier results do not make the next result more favourable.
Try a replacement thought: a losing run creates no promise of a win.
Say your replacement thought slowly. Choose something away from gambling to do next.

activities.title: Make space before acting
activities.description: Try a short pause and an alternative to gambling when an urge appears.
steps: Name the urge without judging it: I am noticing an urge to gamble.
For these few minutes, put off the decision to gamble. Close betting content or move away from it if you can.
Do one simple thing instead: stretch gently, sip water, or notice nearby sounds.
Notice whether the urge changes. It does not have to disappear to finish this practice.
Choose your next step: another pause, a different activity, or contact with someone supportive.

activities.title: Notice your triggers
activities.description: Identify a situation that tends to bring on a gambling urge.
steps: Think of a recent gambling urge that feels manageable to reflect on.
Notice what was happening just before it: a place, a message, a feeling, or a time of day.
Name the thought or feeling that followed. You can use a few words on paper.
Choose one change you could try, such as muting a promotion or planning something for a quiet evening.
Make a small plan: when I notice this cue, I will try this action.

activities.title: Create a coping reminder
activities.description: Prepare a simple reminder to use when thinking clearly feels harder.
steps: On paper, write one personal reason for taking a break from gambling.
Add one action you can take when an urge arrives, such as leaving the situation or doing something else.
Add the name of a supportive person or service you could contact.
Read your reminder slowly. Keep it somewhere easy to reach and imagine using it next time.
